newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 97/98 sugar yield to exceed 10 T/ha - FIRS.
newsitem.headline: French 97/98 sugar yield to exceed 10 T/ha - FIRS.

text.p: French sugar intervention board FIRS predicted on Monday that favourable growing conditions will lift the national 1997/98 beet sugar yield above 10 tonnes per hectare, confirming earlier reports.

"Beet sugar production prospects for 1997/98 are very good. Taking into account a sharp rise in the number of beets per hectare from the previous campaign in particular, the overall feeling, ahead of the (beet test) results of end-July, is that the threshold of 10 tonnes of sugar per hectare...will be exceeded," FIRS said in its July report.
FIRS said 10 tonnes was the yield reached in 1996/97 and the average yield for the last five campaigns.

FIRS also confirmed that it had revised upwards its estimate for 1997/98 sugar beet sowings to 421,000 hectares from a previous forecast of 420,000 hectares. This would represent a 0.24 percent decline from 422,000 hectares planted in 1996/97.
In 1996/97 France produced 4.226 million tonnes of beet sugar.
